cards.a: A WAN that rides DSL, cable, or fiber over a shared access network, almost always using PPPoE as the session/auth layer. It is cheap and everywhere but asymmetric, shared, and less predictable than MPLS.

cards.q: What are the common broadband types and their characteristics?
cards.a: DSL (phone lines, ADSL/VDSL), cable (coax, shared), fiber (GPON/EPON, high speed), and fixed wireless (RF, rural). Fiber is fastest/most symmetric; DSL and cable are asymmetric.

cards.q: What characteristics make broadband a best-effort service?
cards.a: It is asymmetric (download > upload), shared with the neighborhood, has variable latency, low predictability, and no SLA, though it is low cost.

cards.q: What is the session model used on broadband?
cards.a: Access is DSL/cable/fiber, the session layer is PPPoE, authentication is CHAP/RADIUS, and IP is provided via IPCP or DHCP.

cards.q: How do enterprises typically use broadband?
cards.a: As a primary link for small sites, a secondary/backup or DIA link for larger sites, or as cheap SD-WAN transport, with QoS being limited.

cards.q: What is the enterprise broadband playbook for design?
cards.a: Use MTU 1492 for PPPoE, expect the CPE to NAT, use DIA/local breakout, and pair broadband with MPLS for redundancy.

cards.q: Why is the MTU set to 1492 on a broadband link?
cards.a: Because PPPoE adds overhead, so the link MTU must be reduced to 1492.

cards.q: Which commands verify a broadband/PPPoE link?
cards.a: show pppoe session, show interface Dialer1, show ip interface brief, plus ping/traceroute and show nbar for traffic checks.

cards.q: A broadband connection is slow. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A shared/asymmetric link or contention is likely; check bandwidth and latency.

cards.q: No PPPoE session comes up on broadband. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: PPPoE is down; check with show pppoe session.

cards.q: Why is broadband treated as a secondary/DIA or SD-WAN transport rather than a primary SLA link?
cards.a: Because it is asymmetric, shared, best-effort, and has no SLA, so it is not reliable enough alone and is typically paired with MPLS or used for backup/DIA and SD-WAN transport.
